# Xhr appends a second ? to a URL that already has a query

## Context

The keyless Earthquakes tutorial (#6611) loads a Store from a URL that carries its own query: `https://nameless-tundra-27404.herokuapp.com/go/?fn=earthquakes`. Sophie ran it against a packed consumer at dev `d7e91ec544`. The Store's default Xhr pipeline adds `page` and `pageSize`, and the request goes out as:

```
https://nameless-tundra-27404.herokuapp.com/go/?fn=earthquakes?page=1&pageSize=0
```

The service answers HTTP 200 with the body `earthquakes?page=1 is not a function.`, which is not JSON. The bare URL works and returns 76 rows. This blocks #6611's keyless outcome.

## The Problem

`Neo.data.connection.Xhr#request` adds params with `opts.url += ('?' + new URLSearchParams(opts.params).toString())` (`src/data/connection/Xhr.mjs:190` at dev `5f57baeadf`). The `?` is unconditional, so:
- a URL that already has a query gets a second `?`, and the server reads the params as part of the existing value;
- a URL with a `#fragment` gets the params after the `#`, where they never reach the server;
- an empty params object leaves a trailing `?`.

## The Architectural Reality

- `Xhr#request` resolves the URL (`resolveUrl`) and then appends the params. That append is the only `'?' + URLSearchParams` composition in `src/`; `Fetch` never puts params into its URL.
- Store loads reach it through `Xhr#read(params)` → `request({…, params})`.
- `test/playwright/unit/data/connection/UrlResolution.spec.mjs` already stubs `XMLHttpRequest` to capture the URL passed to `open()`. That is the right place to observe the composed request.
- Design authority: n/a. The defect is an observed failure (the error body above), not a contested behavior.

## The Fix

In `src/data/connection/Xhr.mjs`, compose the params into the resolved URL:
- params go before a `#fragment`;
- they join an existing query with `&`, and add no extra separator when the query is empty (`/data?`) or ends in `&`; a `?` inside a query value (`/data?q=why?`) stays part of that value *(narrowed 2026-11-06 from "ends in `?` or `&`", per Emmy's review on #20490)*;
- an empty params object leaves the URL unchanged;
- relative URLs stay relative. Use string composition, not `new URL()`, which needs a base.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A URL with a query gets its params after `&`: `…/go/?fn=earthquakes` + `{page: 1, pageSize: 0}` → `…/go/?fn=earthquakes&page=1&pageSize=0`.
- [ ] A URL with a fragment gets its params before the `#`, with and without an existing query.
- [ ] A URL with no query still gets `?` + params; an empty params object leaves the URL as it is; a relative URL stays relative.
- [ ] Each case is pinned through `Xhr#request` with a recording `XMLHttpRequest` stub, and fails on dev.

## Out of Scope

- #6611's tutorial work and its native acceptance (Sophie keeps both).
- Fetch and Stream, which do not compose params into the URL.
